Check that a network has the structure of a TMFG

Source: R/tmfg.R
tmfg_certificate.Rd

tmfg_certificate() checks that a network from tmfg_network() has the structure of a triangulated maximally filtered graph (TMFG). A TMFG is defined by its structure rather than as the optimum of an objective: for \(p\) variables it is a connected planar graph with exactly \(3(p - 2)\) edges that is chordal (every cycle of four or more nodes has a chord) and is built from four-variable cliques (Massara et al., 2016).

These properties are what make the graph a TMFG and what the LoGo model (logo_network()) relies on, so checking them shows that a returned network is a valid TMFG, for instance that no edge was lost or added. tmfg_certificate() counts how many of the defining properties the network violates.

It returns that count: 0 confirms a valid TMFG.

certificate() reports the same value for a fitted TMFG network. The check does not assess which correlations the construction chose to retain.

Usage

tmfg_certificate(x)

Arguments

x

A TMFG network from tmfg_network() (psychnet).

Value

A single integer from 0 to 4, the number of violated properties; 0 confirms a valid TMFG.

Details

Four properties are checked on the stored graph: the number of edges is \(3(p - 2)\); the graph is chordal, tested by maximum-cardinality search; it is connected; and it is planar. Planarity is decided for any graph by the left-right planarity test (de Fraysseix & Rosenstiehl, 1985; Brandes, 2009), the linear-time test of NetworkX's check_planarity(), which decides the same property as the test of Boyer and Myrvold (2004). Each property is tested on its own, so a graph that breaks several of them, such as \(K_{3,3}\) (too few edges, not chordal, not planar), counts each one.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when x is not a network from tmfg_network().

References

Massara, G. P., Di Matteo, T., & Aste, T. (2016). Network filtering for big data: Triangulated maximally filtered graph. Journal of Complex Networks, 5(2), 161-178. doi:10.1093/comnet/cnw015

de Fraysseix, H., & Rosenstiehl, P. (1985). A characterization of planar graphs by Tremaux orders. Combinatorica, 5(2), 127-135. doi:10.1007/BF02579375

Brandes, U. (2009). The left-right planarity test. Manuscript, University of Konstanz.

Boyer, J. M., & Myrvold, W. J. (2004). On the cutting edge: Simplified O(n) planarity by edge addition. Journal of Graph Algorithms and Applications, 8(3), 241-273. doi:10.7155/jgaa.00091

See also

tmfg_network(); certificate(); lmg_certificate(), the other structural check.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(stats::rnorm(200 * 6), 200, 6)
tmfg_certificate(tmfg_network(x))
#> [1] 0
